meta.name: Compute Atlas
meta.snapshot: Source vintages vary; see each record
meta.coverage: A research collection, not a census of globally available compute
meta.market: Original 2026-08-31 snapshot, not a live verified feed
meta.license: Original model supplied in this conversation; Epoch AI CC BY attribution; Natural Earth public-domain cartography.

companies.name: Amazon / AWS
companies.headline: Custom silicon meets an anchor customer
companies.thesis: Trainium and the Anthropic relationship make hardware choice, customer concentration and capital intensity inseparable.
companies.risk: A campus investment is not a full accelerator bill; customer commitments are not installed capacity.
companies.watch: Commissioning milestones; Trainium utilization; cash investment relative to operating cash flow.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

commitment.notes: Cash PPE is consolidated; AWS H1 net PPE additions $90.120B. Lease/purchase totals include non-data-center categories.

legacy_summary.future_label: Up to 5 GW new capacity signed with Anthropic

companies.name: Alphabet / Google
companies.headline: TPU scale, multiple ways to monetize
companies.thesis: Evaluate external cloud demand alongside internal search and model workloads; a chip-equivalent scalar misses workload fit.
companies.risk: Tenant backstops and third-party capacity can hide outside conventional owned-PPE comparisons.
companies.watch: Cloud cash returns; TPU deployment milestones; uncommenced leases and guarantees.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

commitment.notes: Purchase/other commitments are broad; $24.1B estimated future data-center/energy backstops and $20B private-company capital commitments.

legacy_summary.future_label: 5 GW TPU program from 2027; >1 GW 2026 milestone may overlap

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.headline: Demand can be owned; supply can be leased
companies.thesis: Fairwater, purchased GPU services and customer contracts sit in different parts of the value chain.
companies.risk: Adding internal sites and outsourced supply without delivery mapping double-counts capacity.
companies.watch: Lease commencements; external service margins; site commissioning and cloud monetization.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

commitment.notes: Lease total includes interest; construction commitments $34.566B; uncommenced leases mostly data centers, start FY27-FY33.

legacy_summary.future_label: Firm disclosed/derived outsourced supply; 1 GW demand and 0.7 GW option not additive

companies.name: Meta
companies.headline: The return arrives through the product
companies.thesis: Compute investment is principally evaluated through advertising and product economics, rather than an external cloud price.
companies.risk: A long-lived facility joint venture and a larger regional investment announcement need not cover the same assets.
companies.watch: Advertising uplift; utilization; JV guarantees and cash obligations beyond reported capex.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

commitment.notes: Post-period uncommenced leases include $68B July agreements; do not add to contractual commitments because overlap is likely.

legacy_summary.future_label: Hyperion 5 GW target; internal project target

companies.name: Oracle
companies.headline: Construction risk meets contracted demand
companies.thesis: Distinguish backlog visibility from the liquidity and construction schedule needed to serve it.
companies.risk: Large nominal contracts do not reveal margin, annual delivery profile or future equipment-refresh costs.
companies.watch: Debt and lease funding; prepayments; commissioned capacity against delivery commitments.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

commitment.notes: Uncommenced leases substantially all data centers, start FY27-FY29, 15-19 years; includes $3.3B lessor guarantee. Subsequent $19B purchases excluded.

legacy_summary.future_label: Additional Oracle/OpenAI capacity; >5 GW including Abilene under development

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.headline: The clearest exposure is not the simplest equity
companies.thesis: Underwrite GPU services together with facility leases, OEM financing and customer concentration.
companies.risk: Contracted power, active power and utilized accelerator load describe different stages.
companies.watch: Cash and noncash capex; lease take-on; backlog conversion and accelerator refresh.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

commitment.notes: Cash capex excludes $9.796B noncash PPE liabilities/OEM financing and $8.359B ROU additions. 393 MW site has up to $14.7B payments/16 years.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.headline: Compute is an enabling asset, not the whole thesis
companies.thesis: Assess the infrastructure as an input to autonomy and robotics rather than as direct asset backing for the equity.
companies.risk: Company-wide capex cannot be assigned wholly to AI. A chart-based capacity target is not a site bill of materials.
companies.watch: Compute-specific disclosures; software commercialization; capex allocation.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

commitment.notes: Company-wide capex/OCF; compute is only one use of capital.

legacy_summary.future_label: Visual target to approximately 400 MW by Dec. 2026; not signed cloud capacity

companies.name: Alibaba
companies.headline: A local compute ecosystem with an external cloud business
companies.thesis: Pair cloud monetization with equipment mix and domestic capital commitments; keep native-currency disclosures intact.
companies.risk: One observed Zhangbei campus is not the Alibaba fleet. H20 theoretical throughput is not application performance.
companies.watch: Cloud demand; realization of investment plans; procurement and utilization.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

facts.label: Announced AI/cloud investment plan
facts.note: Plan, not a firm delivered GW inventory.

companies.name: Tencent
companies.headline: Compute supports both applications and cloud
companies.thesis: Evaluate game, advertising and enterprise uses separately; general server infrastructure is not a GPU inventory.
companies.risk: Designed server housing and announced investment cannot establish installed AI MW.
companies.watch: AI-related cash commitments; internal product returns; usable accelerator disclosures.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Baidu
companies.headline: Native compute measures need a precision label
companies.thesis: Cloud and AI infrastructure may be disclosed in P or other compute units without a comparable numerical precision.
companies.risk: Do not convert an unspecified P figure to dense FP8 H100-equivalents.
companies.watch: Workload monetization; chip mix; attributable power and actual deployment.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: ByteDance
companies.headline: Substantial strategic relevance; limited public granularity
companies.thesis: Track as a private operator and potential customer, without fabricating fleet size from spending narratives.
companies.risk: No quantified, facility-mapped inventory is established by the attached reports.
companies.watch: Primary facility disclosures; ownership versus rented compute; power and hardware boundaries.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Huawei
companies.headline: Hardware and cloud are coupled
companies.thesis: Ascend infrastructure connects domestic accelerator supply with cloud deployment; ecosystem maturity affects useful output.
companies.risk: Horinger is a modeled site estimate, not a company-wide installed fleet. Gui’an design scale is not deployed AI capacity.
companies.watch: Ascend deployments; software efficiency; site utilization and disclosure quality.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: China Mobile
companies.headline: Network infrastructure is not all AI compute
companies.thesis: Evaluate telecom cloud capacity separately from general network assets and managed resources.
companies.risk: No owned-accelerator GW bridge is established in the supplied source set.
companies.watch: Precisely defined computing-power disclosures; AI utilization; non-AI capex separation.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: China Telecom
companies.headline: The unit and the ownership boundary matter
companies.thesis: Managed computing resources and company-owned accelerator stock need separate denominators.
companies.risk: Do not translate aggregate cloud resources directly into owned H100-equivalents.
companies.watch: Resource ownership; precision; AI-only capital intensity.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: China Unicom
companies.headline: A capacity distributor as well as an operator
companies.thesis: Distinguish orchestration and network access from ownership of the underlying compute.
companies.risk: Incomplete site disclosure should remain unknown rather than a zero or invented fleet estimate.
companies.watch: Operating versus managed capacity; deployed equipment; power commitments.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: GDS
companies.headline: Real estate economics, not an owned GPU fleet
companies.thesis: For a landlord, utilization, contracted space and customer credit are more meaningful than an invented H100 count.
companies.risk: Data-center area cannot be translated to AI MW without rack density and workload information.
companies.watch: Leasing, utilization, construction cost and tenant concentration.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

facts.label: Q2 revenue / adjusted EBITDA
facts.note: Reported quarterly metrics; adjusted EBITDA is non-GAAP.

facts.label: Area utilization / FY2026 capex guidance
facts.note: Floor-area measure; cannot convert to owned GPU power.

companies.name: VNET
companies.headline: A power and leasing exposure
companies.thesis: Analyze wholesale and retail infrastructure as infrastructure services, separately from tenant accelerators.
companies.risk: Facility power and utilized space are not proof of owned AI compute.
companies.watch: Committed versus utilized capacity; tenant economics and funding.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: SenseTime
companies.headline: Compute service capacity needs unit discipline
companies.thesis: Separate announced computing capacity, precision and realized service revenue.
companies.risk: Lingang and Qianhai announcements establish identifiable projects, not a complete comparable AI fleet.
companies.watch: Utilization; cash conversion; clearly specified precision and equipment.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: xAI / SpaceXAI
companies.headline: Concentrated campus scale
companies.thesis: Large single campuses focus commissioning, energy and workload-utilization risk.
companies.risk: Ownership labels in the original report are historical; no corporate restructuring is verified here.
companies.watch: Power delivery; hardware installation; operating evidence.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.headline: Demand contracts are not owned assets
companies.thesis: Follow each demand commitment through cloud supplier, developer and facility before aggregating capacity.
companies.risk: The same site can appear in a developer announcement, cloud contract and model-customer program.
companies.watch: Delivery schedules; supplier diversification; payment structure.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.headline: Multiple suppliers, overlapping milestones
companies.thesis: Map AWS, Google and Microsoft commitments by timing and service scope, rather than sum headlines.
companies.risk: A future program can contain an earlier milestone. Price, term and power scope can differ.
companies.watch: Phased delivery; utilization; procurement concentration and overlap.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: QTS
companies.headline: Separate the building from its tenant
companies.thesis: Property ownership does not imply ownership of accelerators deployed by a tenant.
companies.risk: Campus targets can overlap downstream cloud and model-company disclosures.
companies.watch: Leasing, delivered critical power and customer concentration.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Crusoe
companies.headline: Development is a separate layer
companies.thesis: Connect construction and power development to cloud operators and end customers.
companies.risk: Abilene expansion records may overlap the Stargate campus program.
companies.watch: Project milestones; construction financing; contracted critical load.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Nebius
companies.headline: Contract visibility with a capacity blind spot
companies.thesis: A large GPU-services contract does not supply a defensible GW denominator where power is undisclosed.
companies.risk: Do not derive capacity from service value alone.
companies.watch: Commissioning; contractual capacity definitions; service economics.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Nscale
companies.headline: Chip count is not installed IT power
companies.thesis: A modeled conversion based on another site is an assumption, not an additional measured GW disclosure.
companies.risk: The original program-level derived power is retained as a model rather than confirmed supply.
companies.watch: Site-specific power; equipment generation; option exercise and delivery.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: IREN
companies.headline: A rare hardware and service cost bridge
companies.thesis: Separate disclosed GPU procurement from multiyear managed-service consideration.
companies.risk: Hardware capex excludes some infrastructure and does not establish a full-fleet economic return.
companies.watch: Deployment milestones; financing; services versus equipment cost.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Galaxy
companies.headline: A landlord behind the GPU cloud
companies.thesis: Helios links facility ownership to CoreWeave’s service business; contractual critical load differs from gross power.
companies.risk: Do not replace 526 MW critical IT with the 800 MW gross envelope.
companies.watch: Phased delivery; lease payments; facility capex and tenant risk.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Fluidstack
companies.headline: A tenant and intermediary in the stack
companies.thesis: Track facility leases and customer arrangements separately from ultimate ownership of chips.
companies.risk: Backstops, capacity reservations and service purchases are different obligations.
companies.watch: Project delivery; guarantees; pass-through power and hardware responsibilities.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

companies.name: Hut 8
companies.headline: A lease benchmark with a third-party backstop
companies.thesis: River Bend exposes the construction and lease layers more clearly than most bundled AI projects.
companies.risk: Google-linked payment support is not Alphabet-owned capex.
companies.watch: Delivered IT capacity; construction spend; tenant credit support.
companies.classification: Analyst synthesis; not a price target

cost_model.basis: Comparable replacement-capital model per IT GW
notes: Epoch's common model prices the same dollars per IT watt across hardware generations; company differences therefore arise through H100e density, not a claimed vendor-specific procurement discount.
Replacement capital is not book value, historical cash capex or a valuation floor.
Observed project, lease, hardware and service benchmarks are kept in separate layers and must not be added without a full scope bridge.
The 'future indicator' column is not uniformly incremental: it mixes signed customer demand, contracted supply and internal target-state projects; its basis is carried company by company.
